refresh_44835_20260810.reasoning:
(a) **Time left until resolution:**
Today is August 10, 2026. The primary election is scheduled for August 11, 2026 (tomorrow), with a potential runoff on August 25, 2026. Thus, resolution occurs within 1-15 days depending on whether a runoff is necessary. This is an extremely short window.

(b) **Status quo outcome if nothing changes:**
Based on the most recent polling data provided (co/efficient poll from July 31 showing Darline Graham at 30%, Fry at 16%, Norman at 15%), if voting patterns align with that final pre-election polling, Darline Graham would win outright. However, multiple polls show varying leaders and suggest a runoff is likely, meaning no candidate will clear 50% + 1 on August 11.

(c) **For each option, the YES resolution scenario:**

- **Pamela Evette**: Wins either the August 11 primary outright (≥50% + 1) or wins the August 25 runoff. Currently not mentioned in any recent polling data provided.
- **Russell Fry**: Wins either the August 11 primary outright or wins the August 25 runoff. Polls range from 12% to 17%.
- **Darline Graham Nordone**: Wins either the August 11 primary outright (appears most likely to do so based on latest polling) or wins the August 25 runoff if forced there. Has Trump endorsement and leads in 2 of 3 recent polls.
- **Henry McMaster**: Wins either the August 11 primary outright or the August 25 runoff. McMaster is currently Governor and is term-limited; no recent polling mentions him as a candidate.
- **Ralph Norman**: Wins either the August 11 primary outright or wins the August 25 runoff. Leads in Emerson poll (22%), second in Trafalgar (17%), third in co/efficient (15%).
- **Mark Lynch**: Wins either the August 11 primary outright or wins the August 25 runoff. Challenged Lindsey Graham in June primary; has support in Spartanburg and Greenville counties. Not mentioned in recent polling data.
- **Other**: Any candidate not listed above wins the primary/runoff.

(d) **Base rate:**
No reliable base rate available — proceeding on priors. However, I can note that in multi-candidate Republican primaries with a runoff provision where polls show a fragmented field and no clear majority, runoffs occur frequently, and the winner is often sensitive to second-choice preferences and turnout dynamics that polls may not fully capture.

(e) **How the live data/research moves me from base rate:**

The research provides three recent polls (Emerson, Trafalgar, co/efficient) taken within days of the election. These are the most current signals available:

1. **Darline Graham Nordone** has consolidated support around Trump's endorsement and is leading or near-leading in all three polls (19%, 27%, 30% respectively). She is the appointed interim Senator and has major institutional backing. The co/efficient poll showing her at 30% is closest to the election and suggests she has the best chance of reaching 50%+1 outright, or winning any runoff.

2. **Ralph Norman** is the second-most-viable candidate based on polling (22%, 17%, 15% across three polls) but consistently below 25%, making an outright win unlikely and a runoff win dependent on second-choice consolidation.

3. **Russell Fry** polls in the 12-17% range—viable but in third tier.

4. **Mark Lynch** is mentioned as having regional support (Spartanburg, Greenville counties) and challenged Lindsey Graham in June, but appears in NO recent polling data provided, suggesting he is either a weaker candidacy or the polls simply don't capture him. This is a red flag for his viability.

5. **Pamela Evette** won the most votes in the gubernatorial primary's first round but lost the runoff to Alan Wilson. No recent polling data places her in the Senate race despite her name being "floated as a possibility"—suggesting she either didn't file or is not gaining traction.

6. **Henry McMaster** is term-limited Governor and no recent reporting suggests he is running. Appointment of his sister to the seat suggests he is supporting her candidacy, not running himself.

7. **Other**: The breadth of possible candidates (Trey Gowdy mentioned, and filing opened July 21-28) means there is non-trivial probability that a candidate outside the listed six wins. However, the listed candidates appear to be the most viable based on name recognition, polling, and media attention.

(f) **How my view has changed since the original forecast:**

The original forecast was:
- Pamela Evette: 14%
- Russell Fry: 17%
- Darline Graham Nordone: 5%
- Henry McMaster: 2%
- Ralph Norman: 16%
- Mark Lynch: 14%
- Other: 32%

That forecast appears to have significantly underweighted **Darline Graham Nordone** (only 5%) and overweighted several others, especially **Evette** (14%) and **Lynch** (14%). The research now shows:

- Darline Graham has Trump's explicit endorsement, leads or is competitive in all three recent polls, and has institutional advantage as the appointed Senator. 5% was far too low.
- Ralph Norman is strong but consistently #1 or #2 and in the 15-22% range, not the sole frontrunner.
- The lack of any polling data for Evette, Lynch, or McMaster as candidates in the special election (vs. gubernatorial race in Evette's case, or generalized floated names) suggests the original forecast gave them too much probability.
- "Other" at 32% may still be defensible given candidate uncertainty, but appears high if the major contenders are indeed limited to Graham, Norman, Fry, and perhaps one or two others.

(g) **If community prediction exists and any option differs >10%, explain why you diverge:**

The original community prediction (which I am asked to review) shows:
- Darline Graham Nordone: 5%
- Ralph Norman: 16%
- Russell Fry: 17%

**My divergences:**

1. **Darline Graham Nordone (was 5%, I assess higher)**: The research shows her leading or co-leading in all three final pre-election polls, with Trump's endorsement, and the advantage of being the appointed incumbent. The co/efficient poll at 30% is within days of the election. 5% is vastly too low. I would move her to 35-45% range as the strongest single candidate.

2. **Ralph Norman (was 16%, I assess similar or slightly lower)**: Consistent polling in the 15-22% range, but always trailing or tied with Graham. His path to victory is narrower (requires a runoff and second-choice consolidation). Keeping at 15-18% seems reasonable.

3. **Russell Fry (was 17%, I assess similar or slightly lower)**: Polls show 12-17%; he is viable but in third tier. I would move slightly down to 13-16%.

4. **Pamela Evette (was 14%, I assess significantly lower)**: No recent polling data places her in the Senate race. The fact that she was defeated in the gubernatorial runoff by Wilson and no polling in this special election mentions her suggests she either did not file or has minimal traction. Moving down to 5-8%.

5. **Mark Lynch (was 14%, I assess slightly lower)**: Mentioned as having regional support but absent from all three recent polls despite being a named June primary challenger to Lindsey Graham. This is concerning for his candidacy. Moving to 8-12%.

6. **Henry McMaster (was 2%, I assess even lower or zero)**: No indication he is running. Moving to 1% or lower.

Following the death of Senator Lindsey Graham on July 11, 2026, a special Republican primary is scheduled for August 11, 2026, to determine the nominee for U.S. Senator from South Carolina. Governor Henry McMaster appointed Darline Graham, Lindsey Graham's younger sister, to complete his term, and she is now seeking the full six-year term with the endorsement of President Donald Trump [thecentersquare.com](https://www.thecentersquare.com/south_carolina/article_7e8eaed0-fd45-4f55-9865-1b9851f238f3.html), [cnn.com](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/01/politics/trump-south-carolina-lindsey-graham-darline-graham).

Polls released in the last week show varying leaders, but suggest a runoff is likely [thecentersquare.com](https://www.thecentersquare.com/south_carolina/article_7e8eaed0-fd45-4f55-9865-1b9851f238f3.html). An Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media poll released Thursday had U.S. Rep. Ralph Norman leading with 22%, followed by Darline Graham at 19%, U.S. Rep. Russell Fry at 12%, and former Governor Mark Sanford at 11% [emersoncollegepolling.com](https://emersoncollegepolling.com/south-carolina-2026-norman-graham-lead-gop-special-primary-runoff-likely/), [charlestoncitypaper.com](https://charlestoncitypaper.com/2026/07/31/norman-graham-lead-early-polling-for-special-gop-senate-primary/). Conversely, a Trafalgar Group poll released Friday showed Darline Graham leading with 27%, with Norman and Fry each at 17% [thecentersquare.com](https://www.thecentersquare.com/south_carolina/article_7e8eaed0-fd45-4f55-9865-1b9851f238f3.html). A co/efficient poll from July 31, 2026, indicated Darline Graham at 30%, Fry at 16%, and Norman at 15% [postandcourier.com](https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/sc-senate-graham-sanford-2026-fry-norman/article_2a9d2b35-0c0c-49fa-ba6c-3ad2aa91d7b2.html).

Other candidates include Mark Lynch, who challenged Lindsey Graham in the June primary, and has significant support in Spartanburg and Greenville Counties [cnn.com](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/01/politics/trump-south-carolina-lindsey-graham-darline-graham), [postandcourier.com](https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/sc-senate-graham-sanford-2026-fry-norman/article_2a9d2b35-0c0c-49fa-ba6c-3ad2aa91d7b2.html). If no candidate reaches 50% plus one vote, a runoff will be held on August 25 [thecentersquare.com](https://www.thecentersquare.com/south_carolina/article_7e8eaed0-fd45-4f55-9865-1b9851f238f3.html).
